title: Investigation of Organized Crime in Interstate Commerce, Hearings, Part 18 (New York and New Jersey), 1950
venue: US Senate Special Committee (Kefauver), via Internet Archive
ask_addressed: mob-tie: Kefauver testimony on the 500 Club
quote: I don't know, but a friend of mine, Paul D'Amato, is the manager there.
summary: Atlantic City witness testimony in 1950 names Paul D'Amato as manager of the 500 Club; the Committee questions witnesses about its back rooms and gambling.
limits: A witness statement, not a Committee finding. I did not find, in the text searched, a finding that the Bruno or any Mafia family controlled the club.

title: 500 Club
quote: operated from the 1930s until the building burned down in 1973.
summary: Built as the 500 Cafe by Phil Barr in the mid-1930s; D'Amato took over in the 1940s and was sole owner by 1949; electrical fire in June 1973. The page notes Summers and Swan claim D'Amato fronted for Reginelli, while a note says Reginelli was a patron, not the owner.
limits: Wikipedia, so context only. Exact 1930 opening year not confirmed (page says 1930s and mid-1930s).

title: Paul D'Amato
quote: Mr. D'Amato was never convicted of a crime, and never spent a day in prison.
summary: States D'Amato was an associate of Chicago and New Orleans mob bosses and that the club was allegedly a gambling front, but he was never convicted.
limits: Wikipedia, so context only. Subject died 1984.

title: A Brief History of the Casino Control Commission
ask_addressed: mob-tie: licensing findings against casino executives
quote: cases in which the Commission found executives unsuitable and required their removal if the companies wanted to be licensed.
summary: The Commission's own history says its 1980 licensing hearings for Caesars and Bally's ended with executives found unsuitable and removed, and that it fined Caesars $257,000 in 1983.
limits: The page does not state the grounds for unsuitability, and does not name organized crime. Confirms the findings, not the mob label.

title: A Brief History of the Casino Control Commission
quote: prior to the opening of Resorts on May 26, 1978.
summary: Resorts opened May 26, 1978 under a temporary permit; the Commission held a six-week full license hearing in late 1978 and early 1979.
limits: Does not describe any finding about organized crime.

title: Caesars World
quote: The association with Malnik earned Caesars three warnings from the Nevada Gaming Commission, and would continue to haunt the brothers.
summary: Says Caesars dealt with Alvin Malnik, identified by federal officials as a Lansky associate, with a Teamsters pension fund loan funding one deal; the NJCCC denied the Perlmans' permanent licences. The ties named are to Lansky's circle, not the Chicago Outfit.
limits: Wikipedia, so context only. The underlying court opinions (In re Boardwalk Regency, 90 N.J. 361) were not opened: justia is blocked.
